A "stress beat" diagram for three words, each shown as a row of circles, one circle per syllable, with the syllable written under each circle. Row 1: "TA – ble": a large dark-orange circle then a small pale circle. Row 2: "ba – NA – na": small, large, small. Row 3: "pho – TO – gra – phy": small, large, small, small. Large circles are and small circles "unstressed (quiet, short, often /ə/)". Clean flat educational illustration, white background, soft colour palette.

A two-column "noun vs verb" chart. Left column header "NOUN: stress first" (soft blue), right column header "VERB: stress second" (soft orange). Four rows, each with a simple icon and the word with capitals: row 1 a vinyl disc icon "REcord" | a microphone icon "reCORD"; row 2 a wrapped gift box "PREsent" | a person handing over a certificate "preSENT"; row 3 a group holding placards "PROtest" | a person raising a hand to object "proTEST"; row 4 a ship with containers "EXport" | an arrow leaving a map of Nigeria "exPORT". Above each word, small beat circles (large for stressed, small for unstressed). Clean flat educational illustration, white background.

A "word family ladder" for the word photograph. Four horizontal steps going up from left to right. On each step, the word is written in syllable blocks with the stressed block in dark orange and the others in pale grey: Step 1 "PHO-to-graph", Step 2 "pho-TO-gra-pher", Step 3 "pho-TO-gra-phy", Step 4 "pho-to-GRA-phic". A small arrow under each word points to the stressed block. Title above: "The stress moves when the word grows". Clean flat educational illustration, white background.
